newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai ended mostly down on Friday due to decreased money demand with trading in two new domestic A share companies listed on Thursday cooling down, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active three-day contract plummeted to 2.21 percent from 12.00 percent on Thursday.
Combined turnover fell to 4.35 million lots from 13.03 million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
"Financial institutions which used to borrow on the repo market bid little today because there was no new listing today and none scheduled for next week," one trader said.
"The fall in early-maturing contracts was also due to normally dull trading before the weekend," he added.

Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly up on a technical rebound in a generally downward trend for weeks so far, traders said. The most active 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 edged up to 121.29 yuan from 120.23 yuan.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market rose to 2.03 million lots from 840,526 lots.
"Prices recovered a little after hitting bottom yesterday and some new investors bought at low levels," one trader said.
Traders expect prices to continue to rise early next week.
